purpose: Improve actual command-only correct acceptance; target at least 30/36 personal positives with unknown and wrong accepts reported separately
hypothesis: Coarse probability cutoffs and grouping errors across distinct finite commands suppress correct personal/benchmark outputs; finer observed score intervals and class-specific policies can improve acceptance with fixed weights and fitting-error limits
changed_factors: original->observed_intent: threshold grid only; observed_intent->observed_class_min2: finite-command grouping with >=2 correct fitting positives
fixed: All model weights, frontend, normalization, 328 commands and their competition, data membership, loss history, UNKNOWN constraints and known-error limits
selection: Maximize correct human fitting accepts under the same empirical error bounds, then synthetic correct. Original policy wins a complete tie. No test/holdout/personal-test prediction used to choose an arm.
qualification: Unchanged; policies are empirically fitted and unqualified. No human support is invented for synthetic-only names.
historical_test_exposure: v1/v2 tests have already been examined. New v3 comparisons are historical regressions, not blind tests; no further tuning after scoring.
primary_target: 30+ correct accepted out of the unchanged 36 synthetic personal command-only positives; wrong accepts/52 negatives and original official/project regressions also reported
wake: Decoupled; preserve the selected Hey Iris model and its existing results
environment: Existing root .venv and local JSON receipts; no new tracking service, Lightning migration, skill installation or environment
